jobs.title: The chorus
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 24, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010; THE CHORUS — crude ballpoint stick figures, round heads, no faces, two then four then six then twelve then thirty, they hold tiny signs and all turn to look at the dog. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: A comments section exists. Wood draws it: stick figures at the back of every panel, commenting. Panel 1: a young man at a bulky computer whose screen shows a comic with two comments beneath it, and two small stick figures drawn at the back of the panel reading over his shoulder, muddy digital flats (in this panel: WOOD, THE CHORUS, BARNABY (the dog)). Stick 1 says "first". Stick 2 says "the dog is good". Panel 2: a young man turning in his chair to address two stick figures standing at the back of his bedroom panel (in this panel: WOOD, THE CHORUS). Wood says "Who are you.". Stick 1 says "readers". Wood says "Where are you from.". Stick 2 says "boise". Panel 3: close-up of a young man staring at a monitor, bemused, monitor glow (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Boise. Seven years in the laundromat and my first readers are in Boise.". Panel 4: a young man drawing at his table while two small stick figures sit on the bed behind him watching, a dog on the floor, no words (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog), THE CHORUS). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chorus_and_meme is the model sheet for THE CHORUS: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @chorus_and_meme for the character the comments section as stick figures at the back of the panel, 2004–2011; four of them get handles in RUST_CODE.BBS / the meme: a stick figure with a four-line helicopter rotor scribbled on its head, hovering six inches, Nov 2006 on; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31.
